plan_item: 77.44.7.A — tablet hover and focus-visible lifecycle across editable PARTIAL element types
finding: The existing representative tablet state lifecycle did not establish interaction-state coverage across every Inspector-editable PARTIAL element type. The expanded matrix also exposed that decorative aria-hidden output must not become keyboard reachable just because focus styles are configured.
change: Expanded tests/browser/editor-inspector-tablet-state-partial-types.test.js so all 44 editable PARTIAL types exercise both tablet hover and focus-visible backgroundColor plus the closed-choice backgroundImage gradient property, through actual Inspector controls and the Canvas, draft, reload, public publish, breakpoint inheritance, reset, and undo/redo lifecycle. Public keyboard-focus assertions remain restricted to semantically focusable nodes, and aria-hidden nodes remain outside keyboard navigation. No runtime code changed.
coverage: 44 editable PARTIAL types; both hover and focus-visible tablet backgroundColor and backgroundImage (closed gradient choices); Inspector states.set property key; Canvas computed color and gradient; draft Save remains unpublished; reload restores both fields; separate Publish applies tablet states; desktop values remain isolated; mobile inherits tablet; tablet reset returns to desktop; Undo/Redo; reset Save preserves published values and reset Publish removes overrides; aria-hidden content remains outside keyboard navigation.
initial_harness_failure: The first full matrix expected every node to receive :focus-visible output. Chromium showed the spacer is intentionally rendered aria-hidden and the public renderer correctly refuses to add it to keyboard navigation. The test was corrected to assert focus-visible behavior on keyboard-focusable semantics and explicitly preserve the decorative aria-hidden exclusion. No product defect was found; no runtime fix was appropriate.
